answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. Consider a pigment as the anchor of the cost.
